title: ELARA's Healthy-Aging Research Reaches Audiences Across Texas
summary: KHOU 11, KENS 5 and CBS19 feature the community input shaping ELARA's research on robots for healthier aging.

sources.label: Read Chorong Park's original LinkedIn post and watch the shared video
KHOU 11: University of Houston tests AI companion robots for older adults
KENS 5: Researchers studying impacts of AI robot companions for older adults
CBS19: AI companion robots could help shape future elder care

paragraphs.text: ELARA's research on robots for healthier aging has reached viewers beyond Houston. In a September 28 update, Chorong Park shared coverage from KHOU 11, KENS 5 and CBS19, highlighting the older adults and student researchers helping shape the work at the University of Houston.

Park described how participants' responses to a robot's appearance, movement, voice and behavior inform questions about comfort, trust and accessibility. The aim is not simply to make a robot appealing, but to understand how it could fit into someone's routines while leaving that person in control.

Her research questions range from emotional connection to medication routines, physical activity and support for people living with chronic conditions. Planned health reminders and privacy controls are directions to investigate, not evidence that the robots already improve health.

For Park, seeing community participants' perspectives reach a wider audience made the coverage especially meaningful. It brings a practical design question into public view: what people want from a robot matters as much as what engineers can make it do.
